identity: SCRIPTURE - Genesis 4:25-5:32 in the Van Dyck Arabic Bible: the birth of Sheth and Enosh, then the genealogy from Adam to Noah (Sheth, Enosh, Qenan, Mahalalel, Yared, Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech, Noah). Eleven printed lines, each holding one verse-paragraph of the genealogy.
law: THE VERSE IS THE UNIT (0k, now confirmed on Luke, on Surat al-Nahl at 100.0, and here). 373 real tokens / 34 ayat-equivalents = 11.0 tokens per verse, the profile of a genealogy chapter. Inside a verse NOTHING cuts - not the w of wa-asha / wa-walada, not the fa of fa-kanat, not the quotation opener qailatan / qailan.
reasoning: The chapter is built from a repeating three-verse formula and the formula IS the verse division: wa-asha X sanatan wa-walada Y | wa-asha X bad ma walada Y ... wa-walada banin wa-banat | fa-kanat kull ayyam X ... wa-mata. Six patriarchs (Sheth, Enosh, Qenan, Mahalalel, Yared, Methuselah) take exactly that shape, so their verse ends are mechanical. Enoch @250-@288 breaks the formula with a fourth verse because wa-sara Akhnukh maa allah replaces wa-asha and then recurs at 5:24 (wa-sara Akhnukh maa allah wa-lam yujad li-anna allah akhadhahu) - the repetition is the tell that these are two different verses, not one. Lamech @323-@370 also takes four because the naming of Noah with its quotation (qailan hadha yuazzina an amalina) is its own verse, 5:29. Adams paragraph takes five because 5:1 and 5:2 precede the formula. 0s applies at full strength: the six identical patriarch paragraphs must be segmented identically, and they are. The one site I argued over is @19/@24 in Gen 4:25, where the Van Dyck printing does put a full stop before li-anna Qayin kana qad qatalahu; I kept the VERSE boundary at @24 and refused the internal one, for two reasons - 0k says the unit is the verse and not the printed sentence, and li-anna is a subordinator that my own rule forbids cutting at (0p/1j). I also refused @9 (qailatan opening the quotation): a speech announcer keeps its quotation when the quote continues on the same line (1v), and in scripture nothing cuts inside a verse anyway.
